source_observation_ecology: Díaz and Kitzberger (2006) reported austral parakeets destructively harvesting flowers of wind-pollinated Nothofagus pumilio for pollen during spring/early summer; occurrence was associated with flowering phenology and altitude.
source_reported_effect: Original source abstract describes substantial flower/pollen harvesting (about 65% reported pollen emptied); this is not a directly estimated 65% reduction in siring fitness.
missing_for_formal_architecture_coding: No matched plant pollen export, stigma deposition, mature-seed fitness or independently heritable structural change was measured in this extracted source; original U6 EVIDENCE_CEILING retained.

source_observation_ecology: Amela García and Hoc (1998) distinguish effective Ptiloglossa tarsata nectar visits contacting anthers and stigma from Augochlorella pollen collection that misses stigma; nectar puncture by Pseudaugochloropsis is a distinct nectar-robbing route. Stigma position changes in successive flower phases.
source_reported_effect: Original flowering phenology describes morning anthesis and three stigma-position phases; this is not a randomized developmental timing or a source-specific new-organ origin experiment.
missing_for_formal_architecture_coding: Do not infer within-genotype reversible phenotype switching from one-way floral maturation, nor conflate nectar robbery with pollen theft, nor infer a structural cost from visit counts.

source_observation_ecology: Bullock, Martínez del Río and Ayala (1989) document pollen as the sole flower reward and a mixture of effective and inefficient bees in Prockia crucis; the pollinator-to-pollen-thief visitor proportion declines during the day.
source_reported_effect: Source abstract reports flower output spanning orders of magnitude among trees and flowering windows around one week; it does not provide a shared-versus-alternative architecture effect.
missing_for_formal_architecture_coding: Visitor classification and time-of-day change are not direct measurements of opposed optima on a manipulated trait coordinate, heritable module costs, or siring-fitness effects; original source EVIDENCE_CEILING retained.

source_observation_ecology: Eguiarte, Martínez del Río and Arita (1987) describe nocturnal nectar-bat pollination and daytime bird, bee and hummingbird visits to Pseudobombax ellipticum; bee pollen collection can interfere with legitimate daytime bird pollination.
source_reported_effect: Original author summary lists several nocturnal bat, day bird, hummingbird and bee guilds; these are pollinator/consumer categories and not independent plant-level treatment replicates.
missing_for_formal_architecture_coding: No comparison of newly constructed timed anther reservoirs versus coexpressed role-dividing organs, and no independently reconstructed historical origin. Primary PDF is a locator; full PDF not reanalyzed in this extraction.

source_observation_ecology: Young (1981, 1985) reports stingless bees collecting cacao pollen without effective stigma contact; 1981 cacao visitor/fruit-set observations and the 1985 pollination discussion concern one taxon, not two independent experimental lineage histories.
source_reported_effect: Original 1981 abstract discusses high Trigona pollen-collection frequency and low measured cacao fruit set; observational female fruit set cannot be assigned solely to architecture genotype or pollen-removal pressure.
missing_for_formal_architecture_coding: Two original articles in one admitted U6 taxon are not two biological taxon records. Actual male siring and viable shared/plastic/fixed structural alternatives were not compared.

source_observation_ecology: Lundgren, Razzak and Wiedenmann (2004) sampled predator-beetle diets, activity and reproduction during maize pollen shed, with pollen as food for Coleomegilla maculata and Harmonia axyridis. This is an ecological food-web record, not in itself pollen stigma transfer or crop siring.
source_reported_effect: Original study compared predatory beetle food use during a defined corn anthesis period with field replicates; direct plant pollen export loss and seed production linked to beetle consumption were not identified in this source extraction.
missing_for_formal_architecture_coding: IMPORTANT FROZEN U6 ADMISSION SOURCE REVIEW: pollen ingested by predatory beetles from shed wind pollen does not itself demonstrate consumptive emasculation or pollen-theft-driven plant fitness harm. Retain original admission unchanged; flag eligibility for independent source review rather than excluding or declaring a negative.
